author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Override Blind Spot
challenge.description: Store managers are overriding order suggestions at an alarming rate because they cannot verify if the model behind them is the one they tested. #model_monica# wants a fully automated registry to ensure every deployment is traceable and reproducible. #requirements_reuben# has a red line: no model enters the registry without a manual, documented review of its evaluation metrics to ensure compliance, so he insists on keeping the process manual.

output.content: I am ready to accept that the model evaluation step stays manual and done by hand, even if it slows down our deployment cycle. I am giving up the speed of a fully automated pipeline in exchange for the certainty that every evaluation metric is thoroughly reviewed before a model enters the registry. If we automate that review, we lose the guarantee that compliance checks are actually performed. I am willing to let the registry itself be fully automated and traceable, but the human sign off on the metrics must stay in the loop. That is the trade I am making: speed in the pipeline for certainty in the validation. I accept the friction of manual review to ensure no unreviewed model reaches production.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are giving up the speed of a fully automated pipeline in exchange for the certainty of thorough manual review, clearly identifying this as a trade-off.
